text:
ashley: Quick follow-up from the routing policy sync — we need a decision on semaphore-style permits (pre-allocated capacity tokens per route) vs per-request scoring (compute score, pick best route). Main constraints: predictable p99 latency, per-tenant region preference, and graceful fallback to cheaper model during overload.

sam: I lean semaphore for predictable headroom. Less compute in hot path, simpler backpressure. But harder to express complex business rules (region preference + tier) as tokens.

marta: product ask: can we expose understandable knobs to customers? tokens = confusing. scoring = easier to explain (score thresholds).

liam: runtime note — with semaphores we avoid extra RPCs to policy eval on each request. But we must map tokens to model variants and KV cache affinity; if token grants model A but we route to model B fallback, cache misses explode.

raj: infra: crossing regions for a score call is expensive and adds tail. If score evals live in control plane, we introduce latency. +1 to semaphore or move scoring to edge.

ashley: what about hybrid: cheap coarse-grained semaphore for capacity + a fast local score for tie-breaks? e.g., token reserves capacity per region/tier, then node picks route with a tiny score (latency/cost). Thoughts?

sam: hybrid seems pragmatic. Implementation questions:
- token granularity (per-gpu, per-pool, per-region)
- token lifecycle (lease TTL, renews)
- fallbacks when tokens exhausted (queue? immediate fallback?)

marta: can we define default policies: best-effort (cheapest), low-latency (priority tokens), privacy (region-locked tokens)? customers pick policy name.

liam: implementation sketch:
```
// reserve
reserveToken(tenant, region, tier) -> tokenID | null
// use
route = chooseLocalRoute(tokenID, payloadHints)
```
If token null -> fallback to score-based scoring async and degrade SLO.

raj: also must consider reading token inventory fast — use local cache with short TTL + invalidate on scale events.

ashley: API contract for policy adapter should be tiny. Proposed:
- reserve(tenant, attrs) -> token
- use(token, request_meta) -> route_id
- release(token)
Return codes: OK, EXPIRED, NO_CAPACITY, INVALID_ATTRS

sam: +1. Keep policy language expression out of hot path; edge nodes get tokens and do lightweight decisions.

marta: UX: surface token exhaustion as a metric and provide a recommended policy per workload. Document the guarantee semantics.

liam: one more ops concern: rollout. need migration plan: start by giving tokens only to a small % of traffic (canary). If OK, progressive rollout.

raj: agree. Also add observability: per-tenant token hit/miss, fallback counts, cost delta.

devops-bot: deploy: routed-policy-adapter v0.3 deployed to staging at 2026-03-20T15:12Z :rocket:

ashley: OK let's capture decisions and action items: 1) build token reserve + local tie-break scoring 2) define adapter contract (ashley+liam) 3) docs + UX (marta) 4) canary rollout plan + metrics (raj). I'll file follow-up RFC.

sam: thanks, putting notes in the architecture board. :thumbsup: 

marta: thanks all.
